source: PM&DC Uniform Curriculum MDCAT-2025 (Final, 26-05-2025); applies to MDCAT-2026 (PM&DC notice 19 May 2026)

los.text: Classify viruses on basis of their structure / number of strands / diseases / hosts.
Identify symptoms, mode of transmission and cause of viral disease (AIDS).
Outline the cellular respiration of proteins and fats and correlate these with that of glucose.
Define and classify biological molecules.
Discuss the importance of biological molecules.
Describe biologically important properties of water (polarity, hydrolysis, specific heat, solvent and reagent, density, cohesion, ionization).
Discuss monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides.
Describe amino acids and the structure of proteins.
Describe phospholipids, triglycerides, alcohols and esters (acylglycerols).
Give an account of structure and function of RNA.
Discuss conjugated molecules (glycolipids, glycoproteins).
Explain the double helical structure of DNA (Watson and Crick).
Define a gene as a sequence of nucleotides coding for a polypeptide.
Compare the structure of typical animal and plant cells.
Compare and contrast prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
Outline structure and function of nucleus, ER, Golgi apparatus and mitochondria.
Describe the structure, chemical composition and function of chromosomes.
Recognize receptors as transducers sensitive to various stimuli.
Explain the structure of a typical neuron.
Define nerve impulse.
Classify reflexes.
Explain the functions of the components of a reflex arc.
Discuss the main parts of the brain.
Describe the functions of each part.
Describe the distinguishing characteristics of enzymes.
Explain the mechanism of action of enzymes.
Describe effects of temperature, pH and concentration on enzyme action.
Describe enzyme inhibitors.
Explain origin of life according to the concept of evolution.
Describe Lamarck's inheritance of acquired characters.
Explain Darwin's theory of natural selection.
Describe the male and female reproductive systems and their regulating hormones.
Describe the menstrual cycle emphasizing the role of hormones.
List common STDs with causative agents and main symptoms.
Describe cartilage, muscle and bone.
Explain the main characteristics and functions of cartilage and bone.
Compare smooth, cardiac and skeletal muscle.
Explain the ultrastructure of skeletal muscle.
Describe the process of skeletal muscle contraction.
Classify joints.
Define arthritis.
Associate inheritance with the laws of Mendel.
Explain the law of independent assortment with an example.
Describe gene linkage and crossing over.
Explain how linkage counters independent assortment and crossing over modifies progeny.
Describe the concept of sex-linkage.
Describe inheritance of sex-linked traits.
Analyze the inheritance of hemophilia.
Discuss the general structure of the human heart.
Describe the phases of heartbeat.
List differences and functions of arteries, veins and capillaries.
Describe the lymphatic system (nodes, vessels, organs).
Define and discuss the functions and importance of specific defence mechanisms.
Discuss the functions of the main parts of the respiratory system.
Discuss gas exchange in human lungs.
Discuss the effect of smoking on the respiratory system.
Describe the parts of the human digestive system.
Explain functions of the main parts including associated structures and glands.
Explain organs of the urinary system; relate kidney structure to function.
Explain glomerular filtration, selective reabsorption and tubular secretion.
Justify kidneys as organs of both excretion and osmoregulation.
Compare glomerular and peritubular capillaries.
Explain causes and treatments of kidney stones.
Outline the causes of kidney failure.
Describe thermoregulation and explain its need.
List nitrogenous compounds excreted.
Describe how biotechnologists produce vaccines.
State the role of biotechnology in diagnosis (DNA/RNA probes, monoclonal antibodies).
Describe products obtained for disease treatment.
Construct mole ratios from balanced equations for use as conversion factors in stoichiometric problems.
Perform stoichiometric calculations with balanced equations using moles, representative particles, masses and volumes of gases (at STP).
Explain the limiting reagent in a reaction.
Calculate the maximum amount of product and the amount of any unreacted excess reagent.
Given any two of theoretical yield, actual yield and percentage yield, calculate the third.
Calculate the theoretical yield and percentage yield from a balanced equation, the amounts of reactants and the actual yield.
Describe the discovery and properties of the proton (positive rays).

topics.name: Planck's quantum theory and the hydrogen spectrum

los.text: Define the photon as a unit of radiation energy.
Describe the hydrogen atom using quantum theory.
Describe the concept of orbitals.
Distinguish among principal energy level, energy sub-level and atomic orbital.
Describe the general shapes of s and p orbitals.
Use the Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion principle and Hund's rule to write electronic configurations.
Write the electronic configuration of atoms.
List the postulates of the kinetic molecular theory.
Describe the motion of gas particles according to kinetic theory.

topics.name: STP, Boyle's and Charles's laws, absolute zero

los.text: State the values of standard temperature and pressure (STP).
Describe the effect of a change in pressure on the volume of a gas.
Describe the effect of a change in temperature on the volume of a gas.
Explain the significance of absolute zero, giving its value.

topics.name: Ideal gas equation and real gases

los.text: Derive the ideal gas equation using Boyle's, Charles's and Avogadro's laws.
Explain the significance and different units of the gas constant R.
Distinguish between real and ideal gases.
Describe simple properties of liquids (diffusion, compression, expansion, molecular motion, intermolecular forces) using kinetic molecular theory.
Explain evaporation, vapour pressure and boiling point.
Describe hydrogen bonding in H₂O, NH₃ and HF.
Explain the anomalous behaviour of water (maximum density at 4 °C).
Describe crystalline solids.
Name three factors that affect the shape of ionic crystals.
Describe ionic and molecular crystals.
Explain the structure of a crystal lattice.
Define lattice energy.

topics.name: Chemical equilibrium and Le Chatelier's principle

los.text: Define chemical equilibrium in terms of a reversible reaction.
Write forward and reverse reactions and describe the macroscopic characteristics of equilibrium.
State Le Chatelier's principle and apply it to changes in concentration, pressure, temperature or catalyst.

topics.name: Solubility product, common ion effect, buffers

los.text: Define and explain the solubility product.
Define and explain the common ion effect with examples.
Define buffer solutions and explain their types.
Explain the synthesis of ammonia by the Haber process.
Define chemical kinetics.
Explain rate of reaction and rate equation.
Explain qualitatively the factors affecting the rate of reaction.

topics.name: Order, activation energy and rate constant

los.text: Give the order with respect to a reactant and write the rate law.
Explain activation energy and activated complex.
Relate activation energy and the activated complex to the rate of reaction.
Describe the role of the rate constant in determining reaction rate.
Define thermodynamics.
Classify reactions as exothermic and endothermic.
Define system, surroundings, boundary, state function, heat, heat capacity, internal energy, work and enthalpy.
Name and define the units of internal energy.

topics.name: First law, Hess's law and enthalpy

los.text: Explain the first law of thermodynamics.
Apply Hess's law to construct simple energy cycles.
Describe the enthalpy of reaction.
Give the characteristics of a redox reaction.
Define oxidation and reduction in terms of change in oxidation number.
Use oxidation-number change to identify atoms oxidised or reduced.
Define cathode, anode, electrode potential and the standard hydrogen electrode.
Define the standard electrode potential of an electrode.
Use VSEPR theory to describe the shapes of molecules.
Describe the features of sigma and pi bonds.
Describe the shapes of simple molecules using orbital hybridisation.
Determine the shapes of molecules from the number of bonded pairs.
Predict molecular polarity from molecular shape.
Explain the ionic character of a covalent bond.
Use molecular polarity to explain physical and chemical properties.
Define bond energy and use it to compare bond strengths.
Define and explain atomic, ionic and covalent radii, ionisation energy, electron affinity, electronegativity, bond energy and bond length.
Recognise the division of the periodic table into s-, p-, d- and f-blocks.
Describe reactions of Group I elements with water, oxygen and chlorine.
Describe reactions of Group II elements with water, oxygen and chlorine.
Describe reactions of Group IV elements.
Describe the electronic structures of d-block elements and their ions.
Define organic chemistry and organic compound.
Classify organic compounds on a structural basis.
Define functional group.
Explain stereoisomerism and its types.
Describe the nomenclature of alkanes.
Define free-radical initiation, propagation and termination.
Describe free-radical substitution in alkanes (methane, ethane).
Explain dehydration of alcohols and dehydrohalogenation of RX for preparing alkenes.
Explain the IUPAC nomenclature of alkenes.
Explain the shape of ethene in terms of sigma and pi C–C bonds.
Describe the structure and reactivity of alkenes (ethene).
Explain the shape of benzene (molecular orbital treatment).
Define resonance, resonance energy and relative stability.
Compare the reactivity of benzene with alkanes and alkenes.
Define addition reactions of benzene and methylbenzene.
Describe the mechanism of electrophilic substitution in benzene.
Discuss nitration, sulphonation, halogenation and Friedel–Crafts alkylation and acylation of benzene and methylbenzene.
Apply the directing effects of substituents in electrophilic substitution of benzene.
Use the IUPAC naming system for alkynes.
Describe the preparation of alkynes by elimination reactions.
Describe the acidity of alkynes.
Discuss hydrogenation, hydrohalogenation and hydration of alkynes.
Describe and distinguish substitution and addition reactions.
Name alkyl halides using the IUPAC system.
Discuss the structure and reactivity of RX.
Describe the mechanisms and types of nucleophilic substitution (SN1, SN2).
Describe the mechanisms and types of elimination (E1, E2).
Explain the nomenclature and structure of alcohols.
Explain the reactivity of alcohols.
Describe the preparation of ethers and esters from alcohols.
Explain the nomenclature, structure and reactivity of phenol.
Discuss the electrophilic aromatic substitution of phenol.
Distinguish between an alcohol and a phenol.
Explain the nomenclature and structure of aldehydes and ketones.
Discuss the preparation of aldehydes and ketones.
Describe and compare the reactivity of aldehydes and ketones.
Describe acid- and base-catalysed nucleophilic addition reactions.
Discuss reduction of aldehydes and ketones to alcohols.
Describe oxidation reactions of aldehydes and ketones.
Describe the nomenclature, structure and preparation of carboxylic acids.
Discuss the reactivity of carboxylic acids.
Describe conversion of carboxylic acids to acyl halides, anhydrides, esters and amides, and their interconversion.
Explain the classification and structure–function relationship of proteins.
Describe the roles of proteins in body functions and their nutritional importance.
Describe the role of enzymes as biocatalysts.
Know the types and applications of adhesives.
Know the types of dyes and their uses.
Know about addition and condensation polymers and their sub-types.
Determine the sum of vectors using perpendicular (rectangular) components.
Describe the scalar product of two vectors in terms of the angle between them.
Describe the vector product of two vectors in terms of the angle between them.
Describe displacement.
Describe the average velocity of objects.
Interpret the displacement–time graph of objects moving along a straight line.
Describe acceleration.
Distinguish between uniform and variable acceleration.
Explain that projectile motion is two-dimensional motion in a vertical plane.
Describe a projectile in the absence of air resistance.
Explain that the horizontal component of velocity is constant.
Explain that the acceleration is vertical and equal to that of a freely falling object.
Differentiate between the horizontal and vertical motions of a projectile.
Use the equations of motion to find a projectile's maximum height, range, position at a given time and time of flight; the launch angle for maximum range and angles giving equal ranges.
Apply Newton's laws to explain the motion of objects in a variety of contexts.
Describe Newton's second law as the rate of change of momentum.
Correlate Newton's third law with conservation of momentum.
Solve problems on elastic and inelastic collisions in one dimension using conservation of momentum.
Describe momentum conservation in explosions.
Identify that in a perfectly elastic collision the relative speed of approach equals the relative speed of separation.
Describe work as the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force.
Describe energy.
Explain kinetic energy.
Explain the difference between potential energy and gravitational potential energy.
Describe that gravitational potential energy is measured from a reference level and can be positive or negative.
Express power as the scalar product of force and velocity.
Explain that work done against friction is dissipated as heat.
State the implications of energy losses in practical devices; efficiency.
Define angular displacement and express it in radians.
Define revolution, degree and radian.
Describe angular velocity.
Relate linear and angular displacement, velocity and acceleration.
Describe the terminal velocity of an object.
Define and explain fluid drag.
Define steady (streamline, laminar), incompressible and non-viscous flow of an ideal fluid.
Explain the transition from laminar to turbulent flow at high velocity.
Describe that most practical fluid flows are turbulent rather than laminar.
Describe the equation of continuity Av = constant and solve problems with it.
Identify the equation of continuity as conservation of mass.
Interpret and apply Bernoulli's effect, including in blood flow.
Derive Bernoulli's equation for a horizontal tube of flow.
Describe how a pressure difference can arise from different rates of flow (Bernoulli's effect).
Describe wave motion as illustrated by vibrations in ropes and springs.
Show that mechanical waves need a medium and electromagnetic waves do not.
Define and apply medium, displacement, amplitude, period, compression, rarefaction, crest, trough, wavelength and velocity.
Solve problems using v = fλ.
Describe energy transfer by a progressive wave.
Compare transverse and longitudinal waves.
Explain that the speed of sound depends on the medium; Newton's formula.
Describe Laplace's correction to Newton's formula.
Identify the factors on which the speed of sound in air depends.
Describe superposition of two waves from coherent sources.
Describe interference of sound waves.
Explain the formation of stationary waves.
Define nodes and antinodes.
Describe the modes of vibration of strings.
Describe stationary waves in vibrating air columns (organ pipes).
Explain the principle of superposition.
Explain simple harmonic motion and its characteristics.
Describe that the projection of uniform circular motion on a diameter is SHM.
Describe that thermal energy flows from higher to lower temperature.
Differentiate between specific heat and molar specific heat.
Calculate work done by a thermodynamic system during a volume change.
Define specific heat and the molar specific heats of a gas.
Describe the first law in terms of change in internal energy, heat supplied and work done.
Explain that the first law expresses conservation of energy.
Apply the first law to derive Cp − Cv = R for an ideal gas.
State Coulomb's law and explain the reduced force in a medium.
Describe the electric field as a field of force.
Calculate the electric field at a point due to two charges of the same or opposite signs.
Describe the field lines of two equal point charges of the same or opposite signs.
Describe the electric field of an infinite charged conducting plate.
Define electric potential at a point as work done per unit positive charge from infinity.
Define the unit of potential.
Derive the expression for the potential due to a point charge.
Describe charging and discharging of a capacitor through a resistance.
Describe steady current.
State Ohm's law.
Define resistivity and explain its dependence on temperature.
Explain the internal resistance of sources and its consequences.
Describe the condition for maximum power transfer.
Define magnetic flux density and its units.
Describe magnetic flux as the scalar product of B and A.
Describe the path of a charged particle shot perpendicular into a magnetic field.
Explain the force on a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field.
State Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.
Use Lenz's law to predict the direction of induced current and relate it to conservation of energy.
Describe the construction and working of a transformer.
Describe how step-up and step-down transformers make power transmission efficient.
Describe the phase of AC and how phase lag and lead occur.
Explain AC through resistors, capacitors and inductors.
Describe the electromagnetic spectrum from radio waves to gamma rays.
Define rectification and describe diodes in half- and full-wave rectification.
Describe the PN junction and its forward and reverse biasing.
Explain the particle model of light in terms of photons with energy.
Describe and explain atomic (line) spectra.
Describe a simple model of the atom with protons, neutrons and electrons.
Identify the spontaneous and random nature of nuclear decay.
Describe half-life and solve problems using λ = 0.693/T½.

topics.name: Biological effects and medical uses of radiation

los.text: Describe the biological effects of radiation and its medical uses.
Scan a passage to answer short questions.
Deduce meanings from the context.
Analyse how a writer or poet uses language that appeals to the senses (figurative language).
Deduce the meaning of difficult words from context clues.
Use synonyms with varying shades of meaning, including for irony, parody and satire.

topics.name: Grammar: pronouns, tenses, verbals, adverbs, prepositions

los.text: Use pronoun–antecedent agreement.
Use tenses correctly.
Use infinitives and infinitive phrases.
Use gerunds and gerund phrases.
Recognise the position of adverbs in sentences according to their kinds.
Use prepositions of position, time, movement and direction.
Use appropriate transitional devices.
Use punctuation marks correctly.
Analyse sentence classes and phrases, and how their position changes meaning.
Recognise and use sentence inversion.
Use active and passive voice appropriately.
Use direct and indirect speech appropriately.
Proofread and edit text for errors of usage and style.
Correct faulty sentence structure.
Apply subject–verb agreement.
Correct errors of word function and spelling.
Develop logical arguments for statements to be true or false.
Give reasons for right beliefs.
Identify and evaluate false beliefs using logical reasoning.
Apply arithmetic operations to number series.
Apply geometric progressions to number series.
Complete letter and symbol series by specific rules.
Predict new relations from given relations.
Build new structures from information in given structures.
Use the result of one problem to resolve another.
Solve puzzles by deductive reasoning.
Gather the different parts of the information given.
Use information to make decisions.
Judge courses of action using arguments.
Give reasons for incidents, events and accidents.
Reject false beliefs through valid arguments.
Build positive thinking through strong arguments.
